unitTests.coverage: HTTP dates in the one format RCTImageCache's formatter reads, NSString integerValue, RCTImageCache's freshness (no-cache, no-store and a component ending in max-age=0 forbid keeping; max-age=N at Date + N; Expires; a tenth of Date - Last-Modified; no stale time without a Date; the byte cache's arrival date), the decoded cache's %g key, the routing of a request by its policy and by what the caches hold (a decoded hit never touches the byte cache), the LRU store (eviction, the entry limit, replacement) and staleness as the caller's judgment

NSURLRequestFromImageSource (method upper-cased, headers replaced without case, a body on any method, the names and values the wire cannot carry), RCTImageLoader's judgment of a download (an empty body before the status, Failed to load <URL>, the response that comes with a failure, repeated headers joined), at most four downloads in first-in-first-out order, cumulative progress coalesced per poll, cancellation outside the transport's poll and listeners, the size limit by Content-Length and by bytes, the idle timeout on an injected clock, an abandoned queued download leaving the queue, stop() silencing every hook after stopping the transport, and hooks that queue more downloads

URI classification (res://, user://, file://, data:, http(s), bare paths), the @Nx scale in a bundled file name, magic-byte sniffing, header dimensions of PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, TGA and SVG, the refusal of absurd headers before any decoder runs, the decode target of RCTTargetSize and the rectangles of the six UIViewContentModes

oracle.independence: Written apart from the probe and from the C++. Reads the server's own log (every request as it arrived on the wire and every answer as it was sent) and the files the server serves, and recomputes what RCTImageLoader, RCTImageCache and NSURLCache do with them: the request's method, headers and body, the failure payloads, the progress semantics, the decoded pictures, the order in which the caches answer, the freshness of a response from its Date, Cache-Control, Expires and Last-Modified, the LRU order and the limits. It replays the 100 operations of the probe over a model of the two caches with the clock each one ran at; where every picture came from, every request the server saw and the keys both caches hold at three checkpoints must agree. Its decode expectations reuse the independent helpers of tests/images-oracle.mjs

notDepartures: A failure's responseCode and httpResponseHeaders reach onError as on iOS: RCTImageLoader.mm:37-46 (addResponseHeadersToError) puts the status and the response's headers in the error's userInfo, the loader's completion applies it at 576-579 to every error that arrives with an NSHTTPURLResponse unless the completion runs on the main queue with data (567-574, not the path of a download), and RCTImageComponentView.mm:195-205 sends them to onError
departuresFromRN: Progress is coalesced to at most one event per request per pump; NSURLSession's data delegate calls the progress block for every chunk, and RCTImageLoader forwards each one
A response served from either cache reports no progress; on iOS NSURLSession hands a cached body to the delegate as data, which the progress block counts

Redirects keep the source's headers (the transport drops only an Authorization header that would cross to another origin); RCTHTTPRequestHandler's redirect delegate lets NSURLSession replace them with the cookies' on iOS, so an app header is dropped there
Only the final 200 is kept in the byte cache, under the URL that was asked for; NSURLCache also keeps the redirect responses
A stale byte-cache entry is downloaded again and never revalidated (no If-None-Match, no 304 handling); Vary, Set-Cookie and Authorization are not considered when a response is kept

prefetch keeps the response in the byte cache only; RCTImageLoader also stores the decoded picture under the key of size 0x0 and scale 1, which no view request has, and the host does not. getSize does not consult the decoded cache either

The byte cache is the host's own: 20 MiB in memory, no entry over 1 MiB, GET without a body and 200 only, and a response without a readable Date is dated by the time it arrived; there is no disk cache, and queryCache answers 'memory' or nothing

The failure text of a transport error comes from the host (Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1:N, unexpected end of stream from H:N, The request timed out.), not from NSURLError; the status and headers that come with a failure are RCTImageLoader's
No cookies, no compression offered (Accept-Encoding is not sent; iOS sends gzip and decodes it), HTTP/1.1 only, and cleartext http is allowed (no App Transport Security)

A response over 128 MiB is refused (by Content-Length or as it arrives) and a download with no bytes for 60 s fails with The request timed out.; RN's loader bounds concurrency, not size, and 60 s is NSURLSession's default request timeout read as an idle timeout
A header name or value the wire cannot carry and a method the transport cannot send fail through onError before any request, with a host-written message

repeat now tiles at the picture's size in points exactly, with a transform under the draw; the old integer-size limit is gone, and the texture is never resized because the decoded cache hands it to every view of the picture
crossOrigin and referrerPolicy become request headers as RN's ImageSourceUtils makes them, and the source headers are used as given
The OS memory warning empties both caches through AppLifecycle; RCTImageCache also clears when the app resigns active, which this host does not do
prefetch and prefetchWithMetadata also accept local sources (resolved without a request); RCTImageLoader's prefetch is a loader request like any other

The limit of four downloads is exact: RCTImageLoader's dequeueTasks (RCTImageLoader.mm:430-437) decrements _activeTasks for every finished task it removes, including a cancelled one that never started, so after such a cancellation iOS can run more than four at once
limits: No disk cache: the byte cache is memory only, so nothing survives the application, and queryCache never answers disk or disk/memory.
No revalidation, Vary handling, cookies, compression, HTTP/2 or HTTP caching of redirects.

tintColor, blurRadius, capInsets, defaultSource, loadingIndicatorSource, fadeDuration, progressiveRenderingEnabled, resizeMethod, resizeMultiplier and overlayColor fail where the Image renders; a border radius on the Image's own style fails too (the host clips rectangles only).
Animated GIF and WebP, nativeImageSource, and an Image inside Text (a failure by design, as for every Control) are not delivered.

The transport and the caches ran against a Node server on loopback (HTTP and HTTPS with a test authority) and the example's own GDScript server; a remote server, a proxy, a captive portal and real network conditions were not exercised.
Assets and network pictures were loaded in the project's own run; no exported app, desktop export or Android export ran.
The captures were taken by the macOS native renderer at content scale 2; the pixel checks sample a few points and there is no independent pixel oracle of the whole frame.
ImageIO's rounding of a thumbnail's size, UIKit's exact tiling geometry, decode memory on a device and the caches' behavior under a real memory warning were not compared with iOS.

Hosted macOS CI has not run this slice; the oracle and the probe state values from what the host delivered or from bounds (four downloads at once, a margin of 20 s around every stale time), never from frame pace or from how the bytes were segmented.
Only macOS arm64 was executed; Windows, Linux, Android, iOS and Web runtimes are not covered.
GF-16 is open: this second slice closes no checkpoint, and no whole GF, other checkpoint, dependency, weight or denominator closes.
